  Child care is an essential service, but paradoxically an under-resourced industry. Thousands of
  families are in need of child care, but most providers are struggling to run a sustainable business.
  The cost of caring for young children exceeds what many families can afford to pay and child care
  workers are left to bear the burden of the disparity, frequently covering the difference in the form
  of tighter profit margins. The average earning of a child care worker in South is $17.82 an hour
  (Zippia, 2023), or about $37,059 a year, meaning they are severely underpaid compared to their
  counterparts in elementary schools. In contrast, the average weekly tuition cost of child care in
  South Gate is about $278 or approximately $1,112 a month. This makes child care the largest
  expense in a families budget, beating rent for the majority of families with multiple children.

  This year, Upwards is running its CDBG-funded program, BOOST, in seven different cities and
  one county in California, Florida, and Washington. BOOST is designed to provide free business
  support services and tools to low-to-moderate income childcare providers. This program treats
  providers as the small business owners they are. It equips them with essential digital tools to
  make their operations more efficient. The goals are to empower them to reach their full revenue
  potential, stabilize their jobs in the childcare industry, and create new childcare jobs – all of which
  lead to more childcare services for the local communities. Upwards piloted this program in 2022 in
  Cathedral City, CA, and is thrilled its success has led to more municipalities adopting the program
  for their residents. For Cathedral City, BOOST assisted 40 LMI daycare providers and 232 LMI
  families.
